**Published online:**
September 8, 2026 (Reuters)

**Geographic focus:**
Global — with primary focus on USA, Japan, China, Euro Zone, Canada, Iran/Middle East

**Temporal focus:**
T1. Historical report [NO]
T2. Forward-looking reporting short-term risks (next few weeks/months) [YES]
T3. Forward-looking reporting long-term risks (next quarters/years) [NO]

**Synopsis:**
As US markets reopen after Labor Day, global calm is disrupted by a surging Japanese yen ahead of an near-certain BOJ rate hike. Japan's upgraded Q2 GDP and a 5-year high in real wages bolster the BOJ case, with fringe speculation of a >25bps move. Yen strength risks reigniting carry trade unwind pressure. Meanwhile, strong global growth (upward GDP revisions in Japan and the Eurozone, solid US August jobs) is pushing the argument for rate hikes globally — including potentially the Fed. Oil is grinding back toward $100 on Iran "economic warfare" rhetoric and Houthi attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure. Copper hit an all-time high. China's exports surged 25% YoY in August, pushing its trade surplus toward $1T annually; its surplus with the US rose to $29B. Canada's retaliatory tariffs on US goods took effect Tuesday. Equity markets are opening in the red as rate and geopolitical pressures converge.

— Strong US August employment, upward global GDP revisions, oil surging toward $100 (inflationary supply shock), and robust growth globally all compound the case for the Fed to hike. The article explicitly states "another series of interest rate rises this month — possibly even at the Federal Reserve." No dovish signals are present. Tone is firmly hawkish.
